text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Bulgaria is expected to select in the next 10 days a contractor to modernise the two biggest reactors at its Kozlodui neuclear power plant, a Kozlodui senior official said.
Two bids have been received for the modernisation of reactors from the Siemens-Framatom-Russia consortium and the U.S. Westinghouse. @
-- Bulgaria's state Bank Consolidation Company (BCC) will launch negotiations for the sale of the control stake in the state owned Expressbank, a BCC senior official said.

-- Sofia municipal authorities are expected to raise on Friday the price of drinking water to 29 levs per cubic metre from 11 levs and to raise two-fold garbage collection taxes, both retroactive from December 1. @

-- Bulgaria's fund "Zemedelie" which provides support for the country's farmers cut interest rates on investment credits to 20 percent of the central interest rate (CIR) from 30 percent, a fund's senior official said. The CIR is now set at 180 percent annually.
-- Bulgaria's Finance minister Dimitar Kostov approached the central bank for some 115 billion lev credit to the government for the planned second revision of the 1996 budget.
-- Balkan countries approved in Istanbul common railway cargo tariffs, effective from February 1. Syria and Iran were also expected to join the common tariff agreement. @
-- Bulgaria's armed forces have run up debts of four billion levs mostly to private and state suppliers of food and uniforms, Defence minister Dimitar Pavlov said.
-- Bulgaria's tourism expects $850 million revenue in 1997, a tourist chamber official said.

-- Bulgaria's Bank Consolidation Company said it expected to settle the sale of a 60 percent stake in the United Bulgarian Bank to the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development by end of the year. @
-- The Sofia City court ruled as insolvent Bulgaria's private FTA financial house. FTA owes 840 million levs to clients while its assets of FTA can cover only one third of the debt.
-- The Bulgarian-Russian oil joint company Rosbulneft raised its capital to two billion levs from 50 million levs, a Rosbulneft senior official said.
